content: Melvin-Koushki reads Ibn Turka as suggesting that comprehensive occult knowledge is simply latent in the Imams and has only begun to be actualized by the author and his circle, a thesis he calls daring, profoundly millenarian in tone, and implying a doctrine of progress. He poses the resulting paradox: how can latter-day knowledge be at once superior to that of the Imams and wholly subsidiary to it?
refers_to_primary: Ibn Turka, R. Shaqq-i Qamar u Bayān-i Sāʿat
